   - `corp_companies` (id, name, slug, created_at) — each RealtimeSuite installation is a "comp [… 4,123 characters omitted]  a guard: create schema `corp` and its own helper functions in the corp schema, not relying on Supabase's `auth.uid()`. But RLS policies on Supabase should use `auth.uid()`. I can do: `create extension if not exists pgcrypto`... hmm, on Supabase `auth.uid()` exists in schema `auth`. To make it testable, I can write the migration to create the `auth` schema/function only if missing? That's hacky.

Better approach: put the corp schema in its own Postgres schema `corp` and define helper `corp.current_user_id()` that wraps `auth.uid()` — defined as `select auth.uid()` ... still needs auth.uid at creation time? No — PL/pgSQL/SQL function bodies are not validated at creation for SQL-language functions? Actually SQL-language functions ARE validated at creation in PG (they're parsed). Hmm, but `check_function_bodies` can be false. Safer: declare the helper as plpgsql, whose bodies aren't validated at creation. So `create or replace function corp.current_user_id() returns uuid language plpgsql stable as $$ begin return auth.uid(); end $$;` — creation succeeds even if auth.uid is missing (deferred), but calling it fails. For local test, that's fine — I can create a stub auth.uid in the scratch DB. The online corporate console for RealtimeSuite installations.

RealtimeSuite runs on a LAN and stays the operational source of truth. Each

```
└──────────────────────────┘                └─────────────┬─────────────┘
                                                          │ anon key + RLS
                                                          ▼
                                                    React console
```

## What corporate users get

| View | What it answers |
| --- | --- |
| Overview | Sites reporting, headcount, who is on shift, month hours and estimated payroll, pending requests, recent discipline |
| Sites & locations | Company profile, locations with time zones, connected sites with sync health and row counts |

### Checking sync

```bash
# manager/admin session on the LAN server
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/api/integrations/corp/status
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/api/integrations/corp/sync

# from the server itself, even while the app is stopped
cd backend && .venv/bin/python -m app.cli corp-sync
```

`status` reports whether sync is configured, the last attempt/success time,
trigger (`startup` / `change` / `interval` / `manual` / `cli`), record counts, the
last error and failure count. If Supabase is unreachable the LAN app is
unaffected — scheduling keeps working and the failure shows up here and in the
console's Sync health view.

`corp/` is a separate hosted app for corporate users. It never talks to a LAN server
directly: RealtimeSuite pushes snapshots to one Supabase project, and the console reads
that project as a signed-in Supabase user. Setup and operations are documented in
[corp/README.md](corp/README.md); the points that matter when changing code:

- **Two credential realms, never mixed.** The console ships `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and the
  public **anon** key; row level security decides what each user reads. The LAN server
  uses the **service_role** key (which bypasses RLS) and it must never reach a browser,
  `frontend/`, `corp/src` or a log line.
- **Schema** — `corp/supabase/migrations/0001_realtimecorp.sql` is applied once in the
  Supabase SQL editor. It creates `corp_companies`, `corp_locations`, `corp_members`,
  `corp_sites`, the snapshot mirrors (`corp_employees`, `corp_work_areas`, `corp_shifts`,
  `corp_tasks`, `corp_time_off_requests`, `corp_exception_requests`,
  `corp_overtime_requests`, `corp_ [… 348 characters omitted] id)`,
  `corp_can_manage` and `corp_is_admin` wrap `corp_members` (roles `corp_admin`,
  `corp_manager`, `corp_viewer`). Mirror tables are read-only to everyone but the service
  role. The UI hides controls by role, but the database is the boundary.
- **`corp_my_scope()`** returns one row per membership (company, location, role) and is what
  the console loads after sign-in. **`corp_bootstrap_company(name, location)`** lets an
  account with no membership create the first company and become its admin.
- **Sync** lives in `backend/app/corp_sync.py`: `COLLECTIONS` maps a collection name to its
  Supabase table and the local SQL that fills it. Adding a mirrored field means editing
  both that SQL and the Supabase column list — the two are not generated from each other.
- **Delivery contract** — every pushed row carries `site_id`, `company_id` and `synced_at`;
  upserts are `POST /rest/v1/<table>?on_conflict=id` with
  `Prefer: resolution=merge-duplicates`, and after a successful pass rows with
  `synced_at < snapshot_start` are deleted for that site. Preserve that ordering: prune only
  after every upsert succeeded, or a partial failure would delete live data.
- **Triggers** — the push worker is woken by a `LISTEN suite_realtime` thread (the same
  trigger fan-out as §8) with a 2 s debounce, plus a full reconciliation every
  `CORP_SYNC_MINUTES`. Any table added to `COLLECTIONS` is picked up automatically, but it
  must have the `suite_notify_row` trigger for change-triggered delivery.
- **Failure is contained**: `sync_now()` never raises to the caller, keeps the last error in
  module state (`GET /api/integrations/corp/status`), records a failed `corp_sync_events`
  row, and never blocks scheduling. Do not make the LAN app depend on network calls.
- **Local development** uses `corp/scripts/mock-supabase.mjs` (`npm run mock` in `corp/`),
  a dev-only stand-in with sample data and no RLS. It is not shipped and must never hold

- **Snapshot window** (change deliberately): shifts/tasks 120 days back + 60 forward,
  requests/notes 180/90 days back, everything else full. Corporate payroll and reports

## What RealtimeCorp is

A separate hosted corporate console (React + Vite + supabase-js) that reads a Supabase project. Each RealtimeSuite installation pushes snapshots of its workforce data into that project; corporate users see the companies, locations and sites they belong to.

Seven views, all backed by real queries: Overview, Sites & locations, People & HR, Operations, Payroll & finance, Policies, Sync health. Admins/managers can edit company details, locations and policies; site data is read-only because the LAN server owns scheduling, clock-in and rates.

- Schema, RLS and helper RPCs: [0001_realtimecorp.sql](corp/supabase/migrations/0001_realtimecorp.sql)
- App entry and routing: [App.tsx](corp/src/App.tsx), data layer [data.ts](corp/src/lib/data.ts), metrics [metrics.ts](corp/src/lib/metrics.ts)
- Setup guide: [corp/README.md](corp/README.md)

## Snapshot sync on the LAN side

[corp_sync.py](backend/app/corp_sync.py) pushes eleven collections — people, work areas, shifts, tasks, time off, exceptions, overtime, discipline, training, board notes, announcements — with source ids and timestamps preserved. It runs at startup, every `CORP_SYNC_MINUTES` (5), and ~2s after any local change, woken by a `LISTEN suite_realtime` thread. Upserts are idempotent on `id`; after a fully successful pass it deletes rows that vanished locally (`synced_at < snapshot_start`), so a partial failure never prunes live data. Three retries with backoff, failures recorded as `corp_sync_events` rows, and the LAN app keeps working offline.

Surfaces: `GET/POST /api/integrations/corp/{status,sync}`, plus `app.cli corp-sync` and `app.cli corp-site-id`.

## Verification

- **SQL**: migration applied twice against a scratch Postgres — 17 tables, RLS on all 17, 23 policies, RPCs callable.
- **Sync**: exercised against a PostgREST stub — 17 requests/11 prunes, `apikey` + merge-duplicates headers, prune URLs use the snapshot timestamp; injected failures retried exactly 3 times; permanent failure returned an error, recorded `failures` and posted a failed sync event.
- **Live backend**: started uvicorn with corp config; startup sync and manual sync succeeded (`ok:true`, 63 shifts), and a local `tasks` update produced a `change`-triggered sync within seconds without waiting for the interval.
- **Console**: typecheck + production build pass; in the browser I signed in, walked all seven views with data, created a location and a policy, switched to the read-only viewer (no editor or edit/delete controls), and completed the first-run company setup for an account with no membership. Pagination was added after noticing PostgREST's 1000-row cap would understate payroll on real volumes.

Not verified: a live hosted Supabase project (no credentials here). RLS is written and syntax-checked but not exercised against Supabase's auth context; that needs your project. The console is served by Vite for preview, not deployed.

## To use it

Create a Supabase project, run the migration in its SQL editor, put the project URL and **anon** key in `corp/.env`, `npm install && npm run dev` in `corp/`, sign in and create your company. Then on the LAN server set `CORP_SUPABASE_URL`, `CORP_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (service_role, server-side only), `CORP_SITE_ID` (from `app.cli corp-site-id`) and `CORP_COMPANY_ID` (shown under Sites & locations), and restart.

## What RealtimeCorp is

A separate hosted corporate console (React + Vite + supabase-js) that reads a Supabase project. Each RealtimeSuite installation pushes snapshots of its workforce data into that project; corporate users see the companies, locations and sites they belong to.

Seven views, all backed by real queries: Overview, Sites & locations, People & HR, Operations, Payroll & finance, Policies, Sync health. Admins/managers can edit company details, locations and policies; site data is read-only because the LAN server owns scheduling, clock-in and rates.

- Schema, RLS and helper RPCs: [0001_realtimecorp.sql](corp/supabase/migrations/0001_realtimecorp.sql)
- App entry and routing: [App.tsx](corp/src/App.tsx), data layer [data.ts](corp/src/lib/data.ts), metrics [metrics.ts](corp/src/lib/metrics.ts)
- Setup guide: [corp/README.md](corp/README.md)

## Snapshot sync on the LAN side

[corp_sync.py](backend/app/corp_sync.py) pushes eleven collections — people, work areas, shifts, tasks, time off, exceptions, overtime, discipline, training, board notes, announcements — with source ids and timestamps preserved. It runs at startup, every `CORP_SYNC_MINUTES` (5), and ~2s after any local change, woken by a `LISTEN suite_realtime` thread. Upserts are idempotent on `id`; after a fully successful pass it deletes rows that vanished locally (`synced_at < snapshot_start`), so a partial failure never prunes live data. Three retries with backoff, failures recorded as `corp_sync_events` rows, and the LAN app keeps working offline.

Surfaces: `GET/POST /api/integrations/corp/{status,sync}`, plus `app.cli corp-sync` and `app.cli corp-site-id`.

## Verification

- **SQL**: migration applied twice against a scratch Postgres — 17 tables, RLS on all 17, 23 policies, RPCs callable.
- **Sync**: exercised against a PostgREST stub — 17 requests/11 prunes, `apikey` + merge-duplicates headers, prune URLs use the snapshot timestamp; injected failures retried exactly 3 times; permanent failure returned an error, recorded `failures` and posted a failed sync event.
- **Live backend**: started uvicorn with corp config; startup sync and manual sync succeeded (`ok:true`, 63 shifts), and a local `tasks` update produced a `change`-triggered sync within seconds without waiting for the interval.
- **Console**: typecheck + production build pass; in the browser I signed in, walked all seven views with data, created a location and a policy, switched to the read-only viewer (no editor or edit/delete controls), and completed the first-run company setup for an account with no membership. Pagination was added after noticing PostgREST's 1000-row cap would understate payroll on real volumes.

{"kind":"tool","id":"i-5HQA4P6LM","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"backend/app/locks.py","instructions":"Add the shared module listing corporate-owned fields and raising 403 on local writes.","content":""""Fields that only RealtimeCorp may change.

Pay, permissions, policy and feature flags are corporate-owned. This module is
the single place that lists them, so every router rejects the same set with the
same message. The lock is unconditional: a site with no corporate connection is
still read-only for these fields (see AGENTS.md, "Corporate-owned controls").

Corporate changes arrive through ``app.corp_commands``; nothing in the LAN app
writes these fields from a local request.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterable

from fastapi import HTTPException

_SUFFIX = " Change it in the RealtimeCorp console; this site applies it within seconds."

_PAY = "Pay rates are managed in RealtimeCorp."
_MULTIPLIER = "Shift pay multipliers are managed in RealtimeCorp."
_PERMISSIONS = "Roles and permissions are managed in RealtimeCorp."
_FEATURES = "Feature flags are managed in RealtimeCorp."
_POLICY = "Organization policy settings are managed in RealtimeCorp."
_TRAINING = "Training mode tuning is managed in RealtimeCorp."

CORP_OWNED_FIELDS: dict[str, str] = {
    "hourly_rate": _PAY,
    "pay_multiplier": _MULTIPLIER,
    "role": _PERMISSIONS,
    "is_training_manager": _PERMISSIONS,
    "admin_training_only": _PERMISSIONS,
    "feature_flags": _FEATURES,
    "training_mode": _TRAINING,
    "enable_extended_leave_lock": _POLICY,
    "extended_leave_threshold_days": _POLICY,
    "enable_retail_floor_simulation": _POLICY,
    "enable_admin_realtime_notifications": _POLICY,
    "default_shift_break_minutes": _POLICY,
    "default_timeline_window_hours": _POLICY,
}

# Organization columns the corporate console may set through a policy command.
CORP_OWNED_ORG_SETTINGS = {
    "enable_extended_leave_lock",
    "extended_leave_threshold_days",
    "enable_retail_floor_simulation",
    "enable_admin_realtime_notifications",
    "default_shift_break_minutes",
    "default_timeline_window_hours",
}


def corp_owned_message(field: str) -> str:
    return CORP_OWNED_FIELDS.get(field, _POLICY)


def reject_corp_owned(payload: dict, fields: Iterable[str] | None = None) -> None:
    """Raise 403 when a local request tries to write a corporate-owned field."""
    keys = list(fields) if fields is not None else list(CORP_OWNED_FIELDS)
    for key in keys:
        if key in payload:
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=403, detail=corp_owned_message(key) + _SUFFIX
            )


def reject_field(payload: dict, field: str) -> None:
    reject_corp_owned(payload, [field])


def corp_managed_payload() -> dict:
    """What the UI needs to explain why a control is read-only."""
    return {
        "locked": True,
        "fields": {key: value + _SUFFIX for key, value in CORP_OWNED_FIELDS.items()},
    }

// The console never writes a site's data directly: it queues an auditable
// command that the site's own server polls and applies.
export async function queueCommand(input: CommandInput): Promise<void> {
  const { data: userData } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
  const { error } = await supabase.from('corp_commands').insert({
    site_id: input.siteId,
    company_id: input.companyId,
    kind: input.kind,
    target_id: input.targetId ?? null,
    payload: input.payload,
    note: input.note ?? null,
    status: 'pending',
    requested_by: userData.user?.id ?? null
  });
  if (error) fail(error.message);
}

export async function cancelCommand(id: string): Promise<void> {
  const { error } = await supabase.rpc('corp_cancel_command', { p_command: id });
  if (error) fail(error.message);
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"i_nnMJ6lF-E","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"corp/src/lib/commands.ts","instructions":"Add helpers for finding a target's queued corporate command and humanizing policy keys.","content":"import type { CorpCommand, CorpCommandKind } from '../types';

// The most recent command of a kind for a target, ignoring cancelled ones. Used
// to show "pending" or "failed" next to the value the site has not applied yet.
export function latestCommand(
  commands: CorpCommand[],
  kind: CorpCommandKind,
  targetId: string | null
): CorpCommand | undefined {
  return commands.find(
    (command) =>
      command.kind === kind &&
      (command.target_id ?? null) === (targetId ?? null) &&
      command.status !== 'cancelled'
  );
}

export function pendingCommand(
  commands: CorpCommand[],
  kind: CorpCommandKind,
  targetId: string | null
): CorpCommand | undefined {
  const latest = latestCommand(commands, kind, targetId);
  return latest && latest.status === 'pending' ? latest : undefined;
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"i_oFJPdLbWY","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"corp/src/components/CommandControls.tsx","instructions":"Add shared rate editor and queued-command badge components.","content":"import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import type { CorpCommand } from '../types';
import { formatDateTime, humanize } from '../lib/format';

// A corporate change the site has not applied yet, or one it rejected.
export function CommandState({ command }: { command?: CorpCommand }) {
  if (!command) return null;
  if (command.status === 'failed') {
    return (
      <span className="badge badge-bad" title={command.error ?? 'The site rejected this change.'}>
        failed
      </span>
    );
  }
  if (command.status !== 'pending') return null;
  return (
    <span className="badge badge-warn" title="Waiting for the site to apply this change">
      pending
    </span>
  );
}

export function CommandError({ command }: { command?: CorpCommand }) {
  if (!command || command.status !== 'failed' || !command.error) return null;
  return (
    <p className="muted small">
      {humanize(command.kind)} failed at {formatDateTime(command.requested_at)}: {command.error}
    </p>
  );
}

/**
 * Hourly rate editor. Saving queues a `set_pay_rate` command; the value on
 * screen only changes once the site applies it and mirrors the new rate back.
 */
export function RateEditor({
  rate,
  command,
  disabled,
  onSave
}: {
  rate: number | string | null;
  command?: CorpCommand;
  disabled?: boolean;
  onSave: (rate: number | null) => Promise<void> | void;
}) {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(rate == null ? '' : String(rate));
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    setValue(rate == null ? '' : String(rate));
  }, [rate]);

  async function save() {
    const raw = value.trim();
    const parsed = raw === '' ? null : Number(raw);
    if (parsed !== null && (!Number.isFinite(parsed) || parsed < 0)) {
      setError('Enter a rate of 0 or more.');
      return;
    }
    setError(null);
    setBusy(true);
    try {
      await onSave(parsed);
    } catch (cause) {
      setError(cause instanceof Error ? cause.message : 'Could not queue the rate change.');
    } finally {
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className="inline-field">
      <input
        type="number"
        min={0}
        step="0.01"
        value={value}
        disabled={disabled || busy}
        onChange={(event) => setValue(event.target.value)}
        aria-label="Hourly rate"
        style={{ width: '92px' }}
      />
      <button
        className="button ghost small"
        type="button"
        disabled={disabled || busy}
        onClick={() => void save()}
      >
        {busy ? '…' : 'Set'}
      </button>
      <CommandState command={command} />
      {error ? <span className="muted small">{error}</span> : null}
    </div>
  );
}
"}}
